thread:
Alex: Heads-up — terraform plan for infra-core is failing after the provider upgrade (v4.2 -> v5.0). Happens in CI and when I run locally. Error below.

Alex: ```
Error: remote-exec provisioner 'command' exited with status 126
  on modules/bootstrap/null_resource.tf line 12, in resource "null_resource" "init-config":
  12: resource "null_resource" "init-config" {

│ stderr: /tmp/init.sh: Permission denied
```

Priya: Which resource address is that? looks like a null_resource?

Alex: It's module.bootstrap.null_resource.init-config[2] — remote-exec runs a small init script copied to /tmp on the instance. Works on current AMI, but after the provider bump the plan now wants to re-run provisioner and fails.

Miguel: Did the AMI change or the user/ssh key? 126 usually permission bits. Can you ssh into the instance and check /tmp/init.sh permissions?

Alex: CI creates instances via image from our pipeline, I spun one up locally and saw init.sh as 000 for some reason. Not sure where that happened.

Janet: Two quick angles: 1) try terraform plan -refresh-only to verify state vs real. 2) If it's a stray permission on the image, reprovision the AMI. Also consider switching to file provisioner + remote-exec with explicit interpreter: ["/bin/bash", "-lc"]. Some distros changed /bin/sh -> dash and scripts fail.

Dan: If CI apply is stuck and blocking, check for a state lock. ci-bot: was there an apply running?

ci-bot: @eng-infra CI pipeline #4523 apply started at 2026-11-01T09:02:14Z, status: failed (provisioner error).

Priya: If the resource exists in state but the instance got recreated externally, you might need to import or taint. Try: 

```
terraform state show module.bootstrap.null_resource.init-config[2]
# or
terraform taint 'module.bootstrap.null_resource.init-config[2]'
```

Miguel: I'd prefer import only if it's actually an external resource with different address. For null_resource import isn't typical — tainting is fine to force re-run. But if the real problem is the AMI packaging pipeline, we should fix that upstream.

Alex: Tainted and re-applied locally, it re-ran but still fails because /tmp/init.sh is created with wrong mode by packer step. So root cause is the AMI build. I'm opening a ticket with images team.

Janet: In the short term, change the provisioner to set mode after upload: 

```
provisioner "file" {
  source = "scripts/init.sh"
  destination = "/tmp/init.sh"
}
provisioner "remote-exec" {
  inline = ["chmod +x /tmp/init.sh", "/tmp/init.sh"]
}
```

That will make the plan deterministic and avoid relying on AMI.

Dan: Also add a small check in CI: run a simple ssh + stat on /tmp/init.sh right after image creation, so we catch it earlier.

Alex: Good call. I'll add the chmod in the TF module and open the image ticket. Thanks all — will follow up when image team responds. :thumbsup:

Priya: If anyone hits the same CI error, ping me and I'll coordinate a hotfix release on the AMI pipeline.

Miguel: Nice narrow root cause. Marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
